title: A rigorous local-volume lower bound for a fixed continuous physical likelihood mixture

physical_model.counts: Integers n_a>=0 and 0<=k_a<=n_a; zero-count arms may be omitted.
physical_model.likelihood: L(theta)=product_a p_a(theta)^k_a * (1-p_a(theta))^(n_a-k_a). This is the likelihood of the realized Bernoulli sequence, without binomial coefficients.

fixed_prior.conditional_B_C: Given A, uniform on the disk B^2+C^2<=m(A)^2, where m(A)=min(A,1-A).
fixed_prior.density: rho(A,B,C)=1/[pi^2*sqrt(A*(1-A))*m(A)^2] on the interior of D.
fixed_prior.normalization: The conditional disk density integrates to one and the marginal A density is the normalized arcsine law. Boundary sets have prior measure zero.
fixed_prior.target_integral: Q=integral_D L(theta)*rho(theta) dtheta. The prior is fixed before observing data.

requirements: V is an invertible real 3x3 matrix, with columns v_j; every d_j is strictly positive. Rational center, matrix and widths are suitable for later exact feasibility checks.
All eight vertices theta0+sum_j epsilon_j*d_j*v_j, epsilon_j in {-1,1}, lie in D. Since D is convex, this implies P is contained in D.
A_lo=A0-sum_j |V_Aj|*d_j and A_hi=A0+sum_j |V_Aj|*d_j satisfy 0<A_lo<=A_hi<1. This sufficient interior condition avoids density-endpoint conventions.
For each observed arm, p0_a=x_a dot theta0, s_a=sum_j |x_a dot v_j|*d_j, p_min_a=p0_a-s_a and p_max_a=p0_a+s_a must satisfy 0<p_min_a<=p_max_a<1.
parallelepiped.density_lower_bound: rho_min=1/[pi^2*sqrt(A_star*(1-A_star))*min(A_star,1-A_star)^2]. A simpler global bound is rho_min>=8/pi^2.

conclusion.integral_bound: Q >= rho_min * 8*|det(V)|*product_j d_j * exp(log L(theta0) - (1/6)*sum_a H_a*sum_j (x_a dot v_j)^2*d_j^2).
conclusion.log_bound: log Q >= log rho_min + log(8*|det(V)|*product_j d_j) + log L(theta0) - (1/6)*sum_a H_a*sum_j (x_a dot v_j)^2*d_j^2.
conclusion.scope: A lower bound for the full fixed-prior integral; not a two-sided enclosure of that integral.

proof: The physical domain is convex because it is the intersection of ||(B,C)||<=A and ||(B,C)||<=1-A. The parallelepiped is the convex hull of its eight vertices, so its vertex checks ensure every line segment used below lies in D.
For ell(theta)=log L(theta), its negative Hessian is sum_a [k_a/p_a(theta)^2+(n_a-k_a)/(1-p_a(theta))^2]*x_a*x_a^T. On P each bracket is at most H_a by the stated probability bounds.
Taylor's theorem along the segment from theta0 to theta0+V*t therefore gives ell(theta0+V*t)>=ell(theta0)+grad ell(theta0) dot V*t-(1/2)*sum_a H_a*(x_a dot V*t)^2.

Under independent uniform t_j on [-d_j,d_j], E[t_j]=0, E[t_i*t_j]=0 for i!=j and E[t_j^2]=d_j^2/3. Thus the expected linear term is zero and E ell(theta0+V*t)>=ell(theta0)-(1/6)*sum_a H_a*sum_j (x_a dot v_j)^2*d_j^2.
The density depends only on A and decreases as A approaches 1/2 from either side: sqrt(A*(1-A))*min(A,1-A)^2 is maximal at the point of [A_lo,A_hi] nearest 1/2. Hence rho(theta)>=rho_min on P.

Retain the nonnegative prior integral over P, apply the density lower bound and the change-of-variables Jacobian |det(V)|, then use Jensen's inequality E exp(ell)>=exp(E ell). These operations give the stated coefficient 1/6 and volume factor.

Choosing theta0, V and d_j after observing the data is valid whenever their geometric conditions are certified: every such bound refers to the same fixed Q. Data selection does not renormalize the prior or replace Q with a data-dependent mixture. The maximum of multiple individually valid lower bounds remains valid.

axis_aligned_specialization.exact_box_feasibility: sqrt((|B0|+d_B)^2+(|C0|+d_C)^2)<=min(A0-d_A,1-A0-d_A). Together with positive widths this is equivalent to containment in D.

anytime_use: For predictable arms, the full fixed-prior Q is a probability law on observation paths. Q/L_true is a nonnegative martingale for interior true models and a supermartingale when the true model has support restrictions.

Use the same Q for both sign hypotheses. Under the true model, a false-direction certificate lower_Q/upper_L_null>=1/delta implies Q/L_true>=1/delta because the false-direction null contains truth. Ville's inequality therefore controls the probability of any wrong-sign certificate, including the zero-signal null, by delta without a factor-two threshold.

An implementation must certify a lower_Q no greater than this bound and a global upper_L_null over the relevant closed physical null. Floating optimizers may propose boxes and null points but do not by themselves certify either side.
limits_and_next_implementation_requireme: This artifact is a mathematical derivation only. No continuum-mixture implementation, outward-rounded numerical certificate, timing result or sampling result is supplied here.
Implement exact or outward vertex/probability feasibility, determinant volume, density constants, center likelihood and curvature arithmetic before using the bound to stop an experiment.

Interior local boxes may avoid the linear-in-n mismatch penalty of a fixed finite grid and yield logarithmic volume penalties under regular identifiable scaling; no uniform regret or sample-complexity theorem is established here.
Near the physical boundary, a feasible full-dimensional box can have very small volume. The stated lower bound can be conservative even if the full continuous mixture is efficient.
Separate treatment is required to exploit probability endpoints with zero matching counts. The present sufficient conditions intentionally keep all observed-arm probabilities in (0,1).
No novelty, superiority over prior work or SOTA status follows from this lemma. Evaluate a frozen implementation with an independent audit and a separately released comparison protocol.
